Cc: Tom Herrera <tom.h@edgelabs.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Short-term credit top-up for throughput validation

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re ready to run a 48-hour throughput validation to reproduce production-like traffic before we finalize the Dedicated sizing. The workload will be steady-state plus two ramp windows (peak ~1,800 QPS, target 95th latency < 250ms).

To run the test with the model variant you recommended (redwood/v2-medium-q4_0), we need a temporary allocation of trial credits or a one-off sandbox top-up that can cover ~2.2M tokens for the run (model + prompt overhead). Timeline: start the window on Thu 14 Jun 00:00 UTC, end Fri 15 Jun 00:00 UTC.

Can your team approve a promo/safety-net top-up (or a short-term quota uplift) that we can consume only for this window? We’re on a tight procurement cycle, so a short-term allowance would unblock the Dedicated sizing decision this week.

I’ve attached our throughput plan (edge_throughput_plan.pdf) with the traffic patterns and target metrics.

Appreciate a quick confirmation — Anita
Anita Shah
Head of Platform Engineering, EdgeLabs

Jordan / Marissa —

I talked to capacity ops. Below are the practical controls we should apply if we approve a 2.5M token promo: 

- Scope to model variant: redwood/v2-medium-q4_0 only.
- Region lock: us-central1 (to keep kernel selection predictable).
- Timebox: 2028-06-14T00:00Z to 2028-06-16T00:00Z (48h window + 24h buffer for logs).
- Token cap: 2.5M, with real-time alert to the account team at 80% usage.
- Fallback: if average 95th latency > 450ms for 15m, auto-throttle to 50% QPS and notify Eng/AE.

Operational risk is low with those controls; the biggest surface is runaway parallelization from the client harness. Recommend approving but require that EdgeLabs share a short-runbook and verify load generator IP range.

If you want, I can prepare a TEMPOffer PDF we can attach to the customer confirming the terms.

-Karthik
